findings.title: Invalid flusher process counts are not rejected and can disable flushing
findings.body: The CLI accepts any integer for --flusher-processes and SpanFlusher performs no validation. A negative value makes num_processes negative at line 60, producing an empty process_to_shards_map and spawning no flusher at all, while submit() finds no backpressure values and continues accepting spans into Redis indefinitely. A value of 0 passed programmatically is also silently changed by `max_processes or len(...)` into one process per shard instead of being rejected or honored. The process count should be validated as >= 1 at the CLI/factory/flusher boundary.

findings.title: join() stops terminating remaining flusher processes after the deadline expires
findings.body: join() sets the shared stopped flag and then iterates over all flusher processes, but if waiting for an early process consumes the deadline, the `break` at lines 339-341 exits the loop before terminate() is attempted for every later process. Those daemon flusher processes can therefore keep polling Redis and producing segments after the strategy has supposedly joined, including after a rebalance or shutdown, and can compete with a replacement flusher for the same shards. All processes should be terminated even when the waiting deadline has already expired.

findings.title: Restarting a hung threaded flusher creates a duplicate flusher for the same shards
findings.body: When produce_to_pipe is used, flushers are threading.Thread objects. _ensure_processes_alive() detects a hang, but the kill at lines 253-257 is skipped because a thread is not a multiprocessing.Process, and _create_process_for_shards() then starts a second thread for the same shards while the hung thread may later resume. Both threads can call flush_segments(), produce the same segment, and call done_flush_segments() for the same shards, risking duplicate buffered segments. Overwriting self.processes[process_index] also loses the only handle to the old thread, so join() can no longer wait for or stop it.

findings.title: Multi-process flusher test never verifies that shared-process shards actually flush
findings.body: test_flusher_processes_limit only asserts the number of processes and that four shard ids appear in process_to_shards_map; it submits no spans and asserts no produced segment for any shard. A regression in the shard-subset SpansBuffer construction, the new SpanFlusher.main() argument order, or flushing when multiple shards share one process/thread would therefore still pass. The test should push spans for shards handled by both processes and assert the flushed output.
